questions.question: Is the position in the sequence part of the input?

result.answer:
Yes. In the visual storyteller, each decoder's first input is the image embedding corresponding to its position in the sequence, so the position's image is part of the input. [1][2][3]
The network takes as input an image I_i from the sequence at every timestep, and the encoder takes the images in order, one at every timestep. [4][5]

questions.question: How is the sequential nature of the story captured?

result.answer:
The encoder processes the images in order, taking one image at every timestep t, so the sequence is encoded step by step. [1][2]
The model uses an LSTM as its first component to summarize the sequence of images; at t=5 it has encoded the 5 images and provides the sequence context through its last hidden state h_e^(t). [3][4]
The model has five independent decoders, one for each image in the sequence; each decoder is initialized with the encoder's last hidden state (the context) and takes the corresponding image embedding as its first input. [5][6]
Each decoder generates a word sequence for its image, and the final story is the concatenation of the outputs of the 5 decoders. [7]
Having a separate decoder for each position lets each decoder learn a position-specific language model (e.g., the first decoder learns opening sentences, the last learns closing sentences). [8][9]

模型用编码器按时间步依次接收图像序列，在t=5时由LSTM的最后一个隐藏状态给出整段序列的上下文向量。 [1][2][3]
该上下文向量用于初始化每个解码器的隐藏状态，每个解码器再以对应图像嵌入作为首个输入。 [4][5][6]
模型包含五个独立解码器，每个图像位置一个，各自生成该位置的词序列，从而为序列每个位置学习特定的语言模型。 [5][7][8]

questions.question: What is the best performing model?

result.answer:
A CNN-based sentence classifier achieved the best results in all three sub-tasks. [1]
The CNN outperformed the RNN model, achieving a macro-F1 score of 0.80. [2]
In another experiment, the CNN system achieved higher performance than the BiLSTM, with a macro-F1 score of 0.69. [3]

supportQuotes.quote: We present baseline experiments using SVMs and neural networks to identify the offensive tweets, discriminate between insults, threats, and profanity, and finally to identify the target of the offensive messages. The results show that this is a challenging task. A CNN-based sentence classifier achieved the best results in all three sub-tasks.

claims.text: A CNN-based sentence classifier achieved the best results in all three sub-tasks.

evaluationProducerReferences.content: We can see that all systems perform significantly better than chance, with the neural models being substantially better than the SVM.
evaluationProducerReferences.sourceTitle: Predicting the Type and Target of Offensive Posts in Social Media

evaluationProducerReferences.content: All systems performed better at identifying target and threats (TIN) than untargeted offenses (UNT).

facets.topic: performed better at identifying target and threats (TIN)

evaluationProducerReferences.content: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first dataset to contain annotation of type and target of offenses in social media and it opens several new avenues for research in this area.
The CNN outperforms the RNN model, achieving a macro-F1 score of 0.80.

We present baseline experiments using SVMs and neural networks to identify the offensive tweets, discriminate between insults, threats, and profanity, and finally to identify the target of the offensive messages. The results show that this is a challenging task. A CNN-based sentence classifier achieved the best results in all three sub-tasks.

conditions: in all three sub-tasks

evaluationProducerReferences.content: All three models achieved similar results far surpassing the random baselines, with a slight performance edge for the neural models.
Using this annotation model, we create a new large publicly available dataset of English tweets.

conditions: Using this annotation model
facets.topic: create a new large publicly available dataset of English tweets

evaluationProducerReferences.content: The CNN system achieved higher performance in this experiment compared to the BiLSTM, with a macro-F1 score of 0.69.
Therefore, we expand on these ideas by proposing a a hierarchical three-level annotation model that encompasses:

facets.topic: proposing a a hierarchical three-level annotation model

evaluationProducerReferences.content: We assess our dataset using traditional and deep learning methods. Our simplest model is a linear SVM trained on word unigrams.

facets.topic: assess our dataset using traditional and deep learning methods

evaluationProducerReferences.content: Finally, we also apply a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model based on the architecture of BIBREF15 , using the same multi-channel inputs as the above BiLSTM.

facets.topic: apply a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model

evaluationProducerReferences.content: Here the systems were trained to distinguish between three targets: a group (GRP), an individual (IND), or others (OTH). All three models achieved similar results far surpassing the random baselines, with a slight performance edge for the neural models.
We set two input channels for the input embedding layers: pre-trained FastText embeddings BIBREF14 , as well as updatable embeddings learned by the model during training.

facets.topic: two input channels for the input embedding layers

evaluationProducerReferences.content: The models are compared against baselines of predicting all labels as the majority or minority classes.
Our models are trained on the training data, and evaluated by predicting the labels for the held-out test set.

Different abusive and offense language identification sub-tasks have been explored in the past few years including aggression identification, bullying detection, hate speech, toxic comments, and offensive language.

facets.topic: abusive and offense language identification sub-tasks

evaluationProducerReferences.content: While each of these sub-tasks tackle a particular type of abuse or offense, they share similar properties and the hierarchical annotation model proposed in this paper aims to capture this.
We evaluate and compare the models using the macro-averaged F1-score as the label distribution is highly imbalanced.

conditions: as the label distribution is highly imbalanced

evaluationProducerReferences.content: In the OLID dataset, we use a hierarchical annotation model split into three levels to distinguish between whether language is offensive or not (A), and type (B) and target (C) of the offensive language.

facets.topic: hierarchical annotation model split into three levels

evaluationProducerReferences.content: However, no prior work has explored the target of the offensive language, which is important in many scenarios, e.g., when studying hate speech with respect to a specific target.

facets.topic: has explored the target of the offensive language

evaluationProducerReferences.content: We also train a bidirectional Long Short-Term-Memory (BiLSTM) model, which we adapted from the sentiment analysis system of sentimentSystem,rasooli2018cross and altered to predict offensive labels instead.
One of them is the one by xu2012learning which apply sentiment analysis to detect bullying in tweets. xu2012learning use topic models to to identify relevant topics in bullying.

facets.topic: apply sentiment analysis to detect bullying in tweets

evaluationProducerReferences.content: Considering that, for example, an insult targeted at an individual is commonly known as cyberbulling and that insults targeted at a group are known as hate speech, we pose that OLID's hierarchical annotation model makes it a useful resource for various offensive language identification sub-tasks.

facets.topic: makes it a useful resource for various offensive language identification sub-tasks

evaluationProducerReferences.content: In OffensEval, each annotation level in OLID is an independent sub-task. The dataset contains 14,100 tweets and is released freely to the research community.

该工作提出多语言无监督语义角色归纳的联合贝叶斯模型，利用平行语料中句子间的词对齐来利用跨语言角色对应关系。 [1][2][3]
模型为每种语言建立单独的贝叶斯模型，并加入跨语言隐变量，以对齐成分间的软角色一致来耦合各语言模型。 [4][5][6]
实验结果显示，加入平行句中的词对齐只带来小幅、不显著的提升，即使源语言已有部分标注数据。 [7]
作者指出，从该平行数据设置中几乎学不到关于语义角色的信息，并认为改进对齐模型是有效利用平行数据进行多语言SRI的必要步骤。 [8][9][10]
按对齐参数的定义，仅8%的英语论元和17%的德语论元是对齐的。 [11]
尚待确认：未记录跨多语言的总体量化汇总或统计显著性结论；仅记录该平行数据设置下提升小且不显著。

supportQuotes.quote: In this paper, we propose a joint Bayesian model for unsupervised semantic role induction in multiple languages.
The multilingual model uses word alignments between sentences in a parallel corpus to exploit role correspondences across languages.
We propose a Bayesian model of semantic role induction (SRI) that uses crosslingual latent variables to capture role alignments in parallel corpora.

claims.text: 该工作提出多语言无监督语义角色归纳的联合贝叶斯模型，利用平行语料中句子间的词对齐来利用跨语言角色对应关系。

supportQuotes.quote: The model consists of individual Bayesian models for each language BIBREF3 , and crosslingual latent variables to incorporate soft role agreement between aligned constituents.
We make copies of the monolingual model for each language and add additional crosslingual latent variables (CLVs) to couple the monolingual models, capturing crosslingual semantic role patterns.
The crosslingual latent variables capture correlations between roles in different languages, and regularize the parameter estimates of the monolingual models.

documents.title: GlossBERT: BERT for Word Sense Disambiguation with Gloss Knowledge

questions.question: How does the neural network architecture accomodate an unknown amount of senses per word?

result.answer:
GlossBERT 通过为目标词在 WordNet 中的所有可能义项构建 context-gloss 对，将 WSD 视为句对分类问题，从而处理每个词数量不定的义项。 [1][2]
测试时，模型输出每个 context-gloss 对的 label=yes 概率，并选择概率最高的义项作为目标词的预测标签。 [3]
记录中给出的示例是每个目标词取全部 N 个可能义项，此处 N=4。 [4]
尚待确认：记录未说明网络架构内部如何编码或聚合数量不定的义项（如池化、注意力或填充机制）。；网络架构内部如何编码或聚合数量不定的义项（如池化、注意力或填充机制）

questions.question: Why masking words in the decoder is helpful?

result.answer:
掩码使精炼解码器在预测第n个精炼词时，依据摘要中的其他词（而非该词本身），从而利用双向上下文。 [1][2]
该过程类似BERT预训练中的完形填空任务，借助上下文语言模型的能力，使解码器生成更流畅、自然的序列。 [3]
从BERT等上下文化嵌入的角度看，精炼解码提供了更完整的输入序列，与其预训练过程一致。 [4]
仅使用左上下文解码器时，预训练语言模型会因上下文不完整、不一致而无法生成足够好的上下文感知词表示，掩码精炼可缓解这一问题。 [5]

questions.question: How are the different components of the model trained? Is it trained end-to-end?

result.answer:
The proposed BERT-based natural language generation model can be trained end-to-end without handcrafted features. [1]
The model uses BERT in both the encoder and decoder of a seq2seq model, with a two-stage decoding structure. [2][3]
During training, the objective is the sum of the two processes, jointly trained using the teacher-forcing algorithm, feeding the ground-truth summary to each decoder. [4]
The model's loss is defined as the sum of the decoder loss and the refine loss. [5]
Training uses an Adam optimizer with learning rate 3e-4 and a dynamic learning rate. [6]
Training settings include batch size 36 and 4 epochs (8 for NYT50), with the best model selected from the last 10 based on development set performance. [7]
Due to GPU memory limits, gradient accumulation is used with accumulate step 12 and 3 samples per step. [8]

questions.question: What is the state of the art described in the paper?

result.answer:
The paper states it is not meant to advance the state of the art on the norms for MPCS. [1]
The paper says its implementation did not explicitly define norms, because the goal was to evaluate the overall architecture, not to enhance the state of the art on norms specification for conversational systems. [2]
The paper describes the state of the art for creating chatbots that can participate in multiparty conversations as currently a combination of research on chatbot creation and research on coordination or governance of multi-agent systems. [3]
The paper states that, to the best of its authors' knowledge, its proposed architecture is the first in the state of the art designed to support the design and development of coordinated aware chatbots in a multiparty conversation. [4]
The paper says that in the state of the art most proposed approaches for context reasoning rely on rules using logics and knowledge bases. [5]
The paper notes a lack of research on chatbot engines directed at building coordination laws integrated with natural language. [6]
尚待确认：No single overall summary of the state of the art is recorded; the paper discusses it across several perspectives and topics.

论文从交互类型、架构类型和上下文推理类型三个视角讨论对话系统的研究现状。 [1]
在上下文推理方面，现有大多数方法依赖使用逻辑和知识库的规则。 [2]
多方可对话聊天机器人（MPCS）的现有研究现状是聊天机器人创建研究与多智能体系统协调或治理研究的结合。 [3]
开发此类系统的最新研究采用了RNN、Dynamic Context-Sensitive Generation和Memory Networks，也评估了HTMM等概率方法。 [4]
Sukhbaatar的工作综述了用RNN或LSTM模型将对话上下文作为序列中长期结构来捕获的研究现状。 [5]
在聊天机器人引擎方面，缺乏将协调规则与自然语言结合的研究。 [6]
论文称其提出的架构是据其所知首个为支持多方可对话中协调感知聊天机器人设计与开发而设计的架构。 [7]
